cuplyr options

Source: R/options.R
cuplyr-options.Rd

Every cuplyr option is set with options() (scope one with withr::local_options()) and, for most, also with an environment variable. The option wins over the environment variable, which wins over the default. cuplyr_options() lists them all with the value in use and where it came from.

Usage

cuplyr_options(internal = FALSE)

Arguments

internal

Also list the internal switches (cuplyr.roll_path, cuplyr.topk_path, cuplyr.check_schema_cache).

Value

cuplyr_options() returns a data frame of class cuplyr_options with one row per option and the character columns option, value (the value cuplyr uses; NA for an unset one), source ("option", "env" or "default"), env_var (NA when there is none) and description. An invalid value is reported as the default, after its warning. Printing it shows the same table.

Options

  • cuplyr.exec_mode (environment variable CUPLYR_EXEC_MODE): "lazy" (the default) or "eager". Whether tbl_gpu() makes lazy tables or runs each verb at once; tbl_gpu(lazy = ) overrides it. See tbl_gpu().

  • cuplyr.fallback: "silent" (the default), "warn" or "error" ("warning" means "warn"). What a CPU fallback does. See cuplyr-fallback.

  • cuplyr.plan_break: "silent" (the default) or "warn". What a plan break does. See cuplyr-fallback.

  • cuplyr.memory_resource (CUPLYR_MEMORY_RESOURCE): "async" (the default), "pool", or "cuda" ("none"; no memory resource). See gpu_memory_state().

  • cuplyr.memory_pool (CUPLYR_MEMORY_POOL): TRUE (the default) or FALSE; 0, "no" and "off" also switch the resource off, and 1, "yes" and "on" on.

  • cuplyr.pool_initial (CUPLYR_POOL_INITIAL): the initial pool size in bytes, 0 or more. Unset: a quarter of the free GPU memory, at most 1 GiB.

  • cuplyr.release_threshold (CUPLYR_RELEASE_THRESHOLD): bytes the async resource keeps before returning memory to the driver, 0 or more. Unset (the default): no automatic release.

  • cuplyr.parquet_pushdown: TRUE (the default) or FALSE. FALSE reads Parquet files without projection and predicate pushdown. See read_parquet_gpu().

  • cuplyr.roll_median (CUPLYR_ROLL_MEDIAN): "exact" (the default) or "frollmedian", the engine of roll_median().

The memory options are read once, when cuplyr is loaded: changing them later has no effect until the next R session.

Internal switches

Listed by cuplyr_options(internal = TRUE); not for normal use.

  • cuplyr.roll_path (CUPLYR_ROLL_PATH): "auto" (the default), "scans" or "cudf"; forces the path of rolling-window functions.

  • cuplyr.topk_path: "auto" (the default), "topk" or "sort"; forces the route of slice_min() and slice_max() (a top-k selection or a full sort).

  • cuplyr.check_schema_cache (CUPLYR_CHECK_SCHEMA_CACHE): TRUE or FALSE (the default); checks the cached schema of every lazy table on use (the environment variable is 1, true or yes).

Invalid values

A value that is not allowed (from the option or the environment variable) warns once per session and value, with class cuplyr_warning_invalid_option (fields option, value and source). The message names the allowed values, and the default is used. A set option decides even when invalid: the environment variable is then not consulted. An invalid value never makes cuplyr_options() or a verb fail; a value that cannot even be inspected (a function, say) is reported as invalid. When warnings are errors (options(warn = 2)), the warning is raised as an error from the call that read the value, naming the option or environment variable, and every later read raises it again until the value is fixed, unless something in between caught the warning and raised it again (a dplyr verb run on the CPU does). A warning counts as given only when its signal returned (one caught by tryCatch(warning = ) is given again on the next read).

A blank option is not invalid. "" means the default, without a warning and without consulting the environment variable, for cuplyr.memory_resource, cuplyr.memory_pool, cuplyr.pool_initial, cuplyr.roll_median and cuplyr.roll_path (NA too for cuplyr.pool_initial). For cuplyr.exec_mode and cuplyr.release_threshold, "" and NA count as unset, so the environment variable decides, as NA does for cuplyr.memory_resource and cuplyr.memory_pool. An environment variable that is empty or only spaces counts as unset for every option: the default is used, without a warning.

cuplyr.memory_resource reads the first element of a vector, as it always did: c("pool", "async") means "pool".

Examples

cuplyr_options()
#> <cuplyr options>
#> cuplyr.exec_mode = lazy  (default, CUPLYR_EXEC_MODE)
#>     Execution mode of new tables: lazy plans (default) or eager, one verb at a time.
#> cuplyr.fallback = silent  (default)
#>     What a CPU fallback does: stay silent, warn, or error.
#> cuplyr.plan_break = silent  (default)
#>     What a plan break does: stay silent or warn.
#> cuplyr.memory_resource = async  (default, CUPLYR_MEMORY_RESOURCE)
#>     GPU memory resource: async (default), pool, or cuda (none). Read at load.
#> cuplyr.memory_pool = TRUE  (default, CUPLYR_MEMORY_POOL)
#>     Set FALSE (or 0, no, off) to use no memory resource. Read at load.
#> cuplyr.pool_initial = <unset>  (default, CUPLYR_POOL_INITIAL)
#>     Initial pool size in bytes (default: a quarter of free GPU memory, at most 1 GiB). Read at load.
#> cuplyr.release_threshold = <unset>  (default, CUPLYR_RELEASE_THRESHOLD)
#>     Bytes the async resource keeps before returning memory to the driver (unset: never). Read at load.
#> cuplyr.parquet_pushdown = TRUE  (default)
#>     Set FALSE to read Parquet files without projection and predicate pushdown.
#> cuplyr.roll_median = exact  (default, CUPLYR_ROLL_MEDIAN)
#>     Engine of roll_median(): exact (default) or frollmedian (data.table).

# Scope an option to a block
withr::with_options(list(cuplyr.fallback = "warn"), {
  # ... a pipeline that should say when it leaves the GPU
})
#> NULL
withr::with_envvar(c(CUPLYR_EXEC_MODE = "eager"), cuplyr_options()[1, ])
#> <cuplyr options>
#> cuplyr.exec_mode = eager  (env, CUPLYR_EXEC_MODE)
#>     Execution mode of new tables: lazy plans (default) or eager, one verb at a time.
